gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-heebo: Bold and loud, Tilt Neon draws tube-like strokes. Heebo sits beneath in a plain sans, tall through the middle, with curves that stop short of closing.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-hind-guntur: Chunky tubes up top, stamped metal below. Hind Guntur keeps its sans-serif strokes uniform and its curve ends well apart from the stems, so paragraphs run along like a steady cable.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-hind-madurai: Hind Madurai fills its lines with lowercase that stands nearly like capitals. Tilt Neon, with its splayed c and tube-like stroke, earns its keep when it goes big and brief.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-hind-mysuru: Commanding Tilt Neon fronts the pair with a splayed c and a large x-height. Hind Mysuru follows in a plain sans whose lowercase presses toward the ascenders, so a long passage hums along without any thinning strokes.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-hind-siliguri: Hind Siliguri has rounds that gap like a cracked bangle, with a flat gray hum of line weight. Hind Siliguri in a plain sans keeps long text steady, while Tilt Neon's tubes shout above it.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-hind-vadodara: Hind Vadodara keeps its sans-serif thickness constant in every direction, with spacious gaps in its rounded glyphs and tall bowls. Tilt Neon is the loud one; Hind Vadodara is the quiet worker.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-huninn: Huninn reads modern and crisp, its lowercase rising close to cap height with s terminals held clear. Huninn in a sans body gives Tilt Neon's tube-like, splayed-c heading something sturdy to stand over.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-karla: Karla reads stocky and friendly, its middle band tall and its c gaping wide. And in a long stretch of text that tall band keeps the lines sturdy, while Tilt Neon holds one stylus-like pressure above.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-kedebideri: Loud tubes above, tall friendly letters below. The strongest quality here is the gap between Tilt Neon's constant ink stripe and Kedebideri's skyward x-height and rounded, open sans-serif shapes.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-khula: Tilt Neon brings stems with no hairlines at all. It makes a big, splayed-c statement, while Khula in a sans does the steady work, its tall belly and open curves carrying the text.
